extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys/agents, and patent examiners involved in preparing or evaluating Information Disclosure Statements (IDSs)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and procedural rules for preparing, formatting, identifying, timing, translating, and filing Information Disclosure Statements (IDSs) under 37 CFR 1.97 and 1.98 (MPEP §609.04). Covers what must be listed/submitted, required copies/translations, timing windows, fees/statements, and exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: List all patents, publications, U.S. applications, or other information
rubrics_metrics.description: Each information disclosure statement must include a list of all patents, publications, U.S. applications, or other information submitted for consideration by the Office (37 CFR 1.98(a)(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The list must be submitted on a separate paper (MPEP §609.04(a) I.). Use forms PTO/SB/08A and 08B to provide the required sections. Applicants are strongly discouraged from submitting completed PTO/SB/08 or PTO-892 forms from other applications since pre-filled examiner initials or other application numbers may confuse the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: IDS list format requirements (page-level and sectional format)
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.98(a)(1) requires (A) a specified format/identification for each page of an IDS, (B) that U.S. patents and U.S. patent application publications be listed in a section separately from citations of other documents, (C) a column providing space next to each document for the examiner’s initials, and (D) a heading that identifies the list as an IDS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate listing of U.S. patents and U.S. patent application publications facilitates OCR and electronic retrieval. Each page should clearly identify the application number (to avoid mixing pages from other applications). A heading on each page indicating 'IDS' promotes proper treatment and reduces handling errors. Forms PTO/SB/08A and 08B provide this format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Per-item identification details (37 CFR 1.98(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Each item in an IDS must be properly identified: U.S. patents by inventor, patent number, and issue date; U.S. patent application publications by applicant, publication number, and publication date; U.S. applications by inventor, eight-digit application number, and filing date; foreign patents/published foreign applications by country/office, document number, and publication date; publications by publisher, author (if any), title, relevant pages, and date/place of publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Date of publication should include at least month and year (year-only accepted in limited circumstances if sufficiently earlier than effective filing date). Pending U.S. applications being cited can be listed under non-patent literature or in a labeled section. Proper identification helps examiners find and consider the cited information.

rubrics_metrics.name: IDS must be submitted on a separate paper (not in the specification)
rubrics_metrics.description: The list of information complying with 37 CFR 1.98(a)(1) and identification requirements of 1.98(b) may not be incorporated into the specification of the application but must be submitted in a separate paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A separate list confirms applicant's intent to submit an IDS and provides an examiner checklist indicating which documents were considered. Use of PTO/SB/08A and 08B is encouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legible copies requirement (37 CFR 1.98(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: An IDS must include legible copies of: (A) each foreign patent; (B) each publication or the portion which caused it to be listed (other than U.S. patents and U.S. patent application publications unless required by the Office); (C) for each cited pending unpublished U.S. application, the application specification including claims and drawings, or that portion which caused it to be listed (unless stored in IFW); and (D) all other information or that portion which caused it to be listed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copies of U.S. patents and U.S. patent application publications are no longer required unless the Office requests them. A pending U.S. application copy requirement is waived if the cited pending application is stored in the USPTO’s Image File Wrapper (IFW) system. Applicants may cite only portions of a pending application (including claims) rather than the entire application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to copy requirement (previously cited in prior application)
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.98(d) states that copies need not be provided if the information was previously cited by or submitted to the Office in a prior application that is properly identified in the IDS, and the prior IDS complied with 37 CFR 1.98(a)-(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If both conditions are met, the examiner will consider the information previously cited in the prior application relied on under 35 U.S.C. 120. This exception does not apply to information cited in an international application under the PCT. If the prior application’s cited information was not in English, a concise explanation of relevance is not required unless the relevance differs from the prior application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cumulative references handling (37 CFR 1.98(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: When two or more patents or publications listed are substantively cumulative, a copy of one may be submitted without copies of the others if a statement is made that the others are cumulative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner will consider only the copy submitted and may cross out cumulative listings on form PTO/SB/08. However, case law (Semiconductor Energy Laboratory Co. v. Samsung) cautions that a withheld reference may still be highly material if it discloses a more complete combination of claimed elements even if other references are before the examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translations and concise explanation for non-English information (37 CFR 1.98(a)(3)(ii) and III)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a written English translation of a non-English document is within the possession, custody or control of, or readily available to, an individual designated in 37 CFR 1.56(c), a copy of the translation must accompany the statement. Each IDS must include a concise explanation of relevance for information not in English as presently understood by the designated individual.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a complete English translation is submitted, no concise explanation is required. An English-language abstract or an English-language version of a foreign search report/action indicating relevance can satisfy the requirement. The concise explanation may point to specific figures/paragraphs and need only indicate relevance; however, applicants must not intentionally omit key teachings or submit partial translations/explanations that they know will misdirect the examiner (see Semiconductor Energy Laboratory decision). Translations need not be verified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic filing limitations for IDSs
rubrics_metrics.description: Electronic means for filing IDSs are not permitted except for (A) citations to U.S. patents, U.S. patent application publications, foreign patent documents and non-patent literature in an IDS filed via the USPTO’s Electronic Filing System (EFS) (MPEP §609.07); or (B) a compact disc (CD) that has tables, sequence listings, or program listings included in a paper IDS in compliance with 37 CFR 1.52(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A CD cannot be used to submit the IDS listing or copies of the documents cited in the IDS. Follow MPEP §609.07 for EFS submission rules for permitted categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concise explanation limited to non-English information (scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: The concise explanation requirement is limited to information not in the English language and is limited to the relevance as understood by the designated individual at the time the information is submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are encouraged (but not required) to provide concise explanations for English-language information as well, especially for long/complex documents or when a particular portion is highly relevant. Pointing out relevant pages/lines is helpful to the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing: IDS filed within 3 months of filing or before first Office action (37 CFR 1.97(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: An IDS will be considered by the examiner if filed within 3 months of filing (for national apps) or before the mailing of a first Office action on the merits; for international apps, within 3 months of entry of national stage or before first Office action on the merits; for RCEs and CPAs, before the mailing of a first Office action on the merits. IDSs filed in these periods require neither a fee nor a statement under 37 CFR 1.97(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An IDS filed within these periods is considered filed on receipt date (or earlier mailing date with proper certificate). If the last day falls on weekend/holiday, filing on next business day is timely. Even if a final action/notice of allowance/Quayle action is mailed prior to the 3-month date, a complete IDS filed within the 3-month window will be considered. An examiner should not make a first Office action final in a continuing application if information submitted in this period is used in a new ground of rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'first Office action on the merits' and measurement of timing
rubrics_metrics.description: An action on the merits treats patentability (e.g., rejection or indication of allowability) rather than merely formal/procedural matters. For timing, the 3-month window for national applications is measured from the actual filing date, and for international applications from the date of entry of the national stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: restriction requirements or fee requirements are not actions on the merits. Use these definitions to assess whether an IDS is timely under 37 CFR 1.97(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: IDS timing and special rules for RCEs and CPAs
rubrics_metrics.description: The 3-month window does not apply to RCEs filed under 37 CFR 1.114 or CPAs filed under 37 CFR 1.53(d); an IDS filed after an RCE will be considered if filed before the mailing date of a first Office action on the merits. Applicants are encouraged to file any IDS with the filing of a RCE or as early as possible in a CPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because RCEs are treated as amended applications with short turnover times, early filing of IDSs is recommended. If IDS cannot be filed before the first Office action after an RCE/CPA, applicants may request a 3-month suspension of action under 37 CFR 1.103(b)/(c) and are requested to notify the examiner when submitting an IDS near the end of such suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: IDS filed after initial window but before prosecution closes (37 CFR 1.97(c)) — statement or fee required
rubrics_metrics.description: An IDS filed after the initial periods but before prosecution closes (i.e., before final Office action, Notice of Allowance, or Ex parte Quayle action) will be considered only if accompanied by either (1) a statement as specified in 37 CFR 1.97(e) or (2) the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(p).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If information submitted with a 1.97(e) statement is used in a new ground of rejection on unamended claims, the next Office action will not be made final (applicant is deemed to have submitted promptly). If the new ground of rejection was necessitated by applicant amendment, the next action can be final. If applicant pays the fee under 1.17(p) during this period, the examiner may use the information and make the next Office action final, provided no other new ground not necessitated by amendment is introduced.

rubrics_metrics.name: IDS filed after prosecution closes but before payment of issue fee (37 CFR 1.97(d)) — statement and fee required
rubrics_metrics.description: An IDS filed on or after mailing of a final action/notice of allowance/ex parte Quayle action but before or simultaneous with payment of the issue fee will be considered only if accompanied by (A) a statement as specified in 37 CFR 1.97(e) and (B) the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(p).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These requirements reflect the late stage of prosecution. Form paragraph 6.52 may be used to inform applicant that the IDS is being considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: IDS filed after payment of issue fee — not considered unless withdrawn from issue
rubrics_metrics.description: Information disclosure statements filed after payment of the issue fee will not be considered but will be placed in the application file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may withdraw the application from issue by petition under 37 CFR 1.313(c) and file a RCE or continuing application to have the information considered. The petition can be filed under different 1.313(c) subsections depending on the circumstances (e.g., unequivocal statement of unpatentability of claims over the information). Applicants are encouraged to call the Office of Petitions to determine timing feasibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver for copies when cited pending U.S. application is stored in IFW
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirement for a legible copy of the specification (including claims and drawings) of each cited pending U.S. application is sua sponte waived where the cited pending application is stored in the USPTO’s Image File Wrapper (IFW) system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the cited pending U.S. application is in IFW, no copy need be provided. A pending U.S. application identified only in the specification’s background rather than separately on an IDS listing is not part of an IDS submission and the 1.98(a)(2)(iii) supply requirement is not applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concise explanation may indicate relevant portions and need not discuss differences
rubrics_metrics.description: The concise explanation of relevance for non-English information may indicate that a particular figure or paragraph is relevant and may be a simple statement pointing to similarities. It is permissible but not necessary to discuss differences between the cited information and the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concise explanations that point out relevant pages/lines are particularly helpful. However, applicants must not omit key teachings or provide partial translations/explanations that misdirect the examiner (Semiconductor Energy Laboratory decision).

rubrics_metrics.name: When prior foreign office search report can satisfy concise explanation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Where non-English information was cited in a foreign patent office search report or other action in a counterpart foreign application, the requirement for a concise explanation of relevance can be satisfied by submitting an English-language version of that search report or action indicating the degree/portion of relevance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The English-language version may indicate which portion of the reference is relevant, to which claims, or an 'X', 'Y', or 'A' marking. A mere statement that a reference was cited in prosecution of a U.S. application (not relied on under 35 U.S.C. 120) does not satisfy the requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness standard tied to knowledge of designated individual (reasonable time)
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirements of 37 CFR 1.97 provide for consideration by the Office of information submitted within a reasonable time — i.e., within 3 months after an individual designated in 37 CFR 1.56(c) becomes aware of the information or within 3 months of the information being cited by a foreign office in a counterpart application — up until the point the issue fee is paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant cannot comply with 1.97(d) timing, they may file a RCE or continuing application to have the information considered. The parent application could be permitted to become abandoned in such cases.
